question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Tangent or Cotangent Curve
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943521/assets/c2e5b01cf03f1f9d82562ee51fc484448e90b74dd2584daf18a499849ca36bff.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
question.worked_solution:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}+C) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{1}{3}(x+3C))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+3C$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{1}{3}(x+3C))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943521/assets/29346a073d6a22f0bab74eeac86431e8c761c9ed21a005ec6965f71e6436c117.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3})$ by $\frac{7\pi }{4}-\frac{3\pi }{2}=\frac{\pi }{4}$ units to the right. Therefore:

$$
3C=-\frac{\pi }{4}\,⟹\,C=-\frac{\pi }{12}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $-\frac{\pi }{12}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $-\frac{\pi }{12}.$
